context: A uni student interviews a retired farmer about land changes
purpose: Teach: 仮想/カルチャー/娯楽/野生/広域/頻度/産地/石炭

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間いただきありがとうございます。まず、昔この辺りはどんな産地として知られていましたか？
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. First, what was this area known for producing back then?
lines.style: Polite university student opening an academic interview with formal gratitude and clear research framing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うちは米だがな、山の向こうは石炭の町だった。冬は石炭ストーブの煙で空が灰色だったよ。
lines.en: We grew rice, but past the mountain was a coal town. In winter the sky was grey from coal stove smoke.
lines.style: Elderly farmer reminiscing warmly, slow deliberate pace with sensory recollection of childhood landscape.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: そうだったんですね。当時、野生動物が畑に出てくる頻度はどのくらいでしたか？
lines.en: I see. Back then, how often did wild animals come into the fields?
lines.style: Curious researcher pivoting to ecological questions with respectful follow-up tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今より少なかったな。人がもっと山に入って、狩りもしてたから。最近は熊が広域に降りてくる。
lines.en: Less than now. People went into the mountains more, did hunting too. Lately bears come down over a wide area.
lines.style: Reflective elder contrasting past and present with mild concern about modern wildlife encroachment.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 村の娯楽というと、当時は何があったんですか？
lines.en: What kind of entertainment did the village have back then?
lines.style: Student shifting gently to cultural questions, genuine youthful curiosity in tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 娯楽なんて盆踊りくらいさ。今の若いもんは仮想空間で遊ぶんだろ？わしには分からん世界だ。
lines.en: Entertainment was just the Bon dance. Young folks today play in virtual spaces, right? A world I don't understand.
lines.style: Chuckling grandfather, self-deprecating about technology gap, affectionate teasing of younger generation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 正直、僕も初めて田舎に来てカルチャーショックを受けました。土地の使い方が全然違って。
lines.en: Honestly, coming to the countryside was a culture shock for me. The way land is used is completely different.
lines.style: Earnest admission from student, building rapport through personal vulnerability and observation.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そりゃそうだ。昔は一枚一枚の田んぼに名前があった。今は誰も覚えとらん。
lines.en: Of course. Each rice paddy used to have its own name. Nobody remembers now.
lines.style: Wistful elder voicing quiet grief over lost local knowledge and intimate land relationships.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: その名前、ぜひ記録させてください。貴重なお話、本当にありがとうございます。
lines.en: Please let me record those names. This is invaluable, thank you so much.
lines.style: Animated student recognizing research gold, sincere gratitude tinged with academic excitement.
